It combines an ESP32-based wearable device with multiple sensors and a mobile application to collect, transmit, and visualize physiological and environmental readings in real time. details:
OrbitCare – Smart Wearable Health Monitoring for Astronauts

Project Overview

OrbitCare is a smart wearable health monitoring prototype developed in response to NASA's challenge, "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions."

1. The Problem

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to challenging conditions, including microgravity, isolation, and changes in the space environment. Monitoring physiological indicators and physical activity is important for maintaining awareness of astronauts' health throughout their missions.

OrbitCare addresses the need for an integrated monitoring system that can collect and track different health-related indicators through a wearable device and a dedicated software platform.

2. Our Solution

OrbitCare combines a wearable device with a dedicated mobile application to collect, transmit, visualize, and monitor physiological, movement, and environmental readings.

The wearable device continuously collects sensor data, while the mobile application provides a centralized dashboard for monitoring readings, tracking changes, and identifying deviations from individual baseline values.

3. Hardware Components

The prototype uses an ESP32 microcontroller connected to multiple sensors and components:

  • MAX30102: Estimates heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2).
  • MPU6050: Tracks movement, acceleration, and orientation.
  • DHT11: Measures surrounding temperature and humidity.
  • OLED Display: Displays sensor readings directly on the wearable device.
  • Buzzer: Provides audible alerts when readings deviate from configured baseline values.

4. Software Architecture

OrbitCare uses an integrated software architecture connecting the wearable device to a mobile monitoring platform.

  1. Sensors collect physiological, movement, and environmental readings.
  2. The ESP32 processes the readings and transmits them over Wi-Fi.
  3. A Python FastAPI backend receives and manages the incoming data.
  4. A React Native mobile application, developed using Expo, displays the information through a monitoring dashboard.
  5. The application monitors incoming readings and identifies deviations from user-configured baseline values.

5. Personalized Baseline Monitoring and Intelligent Alerts

One of OrbitCare's main features is its personalized baseline monitoring system.

Instead of relying only on fixed values shared by everyone, OrbitCare uses user-configured baseline values as individual reference points for monitoring.

The system works through the following process:

  • Personal Baseline: Reference values are configured for the individual user.
  • Continuous Monitoring: The wearable device collects sensor readings continuously.
  • Baseline Comparison: The application compares incoming readings against the user's configured baseline ranges.
  • Deviation Detection: When a reading moves outside its configured acceptable range, the system identifies the deviation.
  • Visual Alerts: The mobile application displays an alert to highlight the detected change.
  • Audible Alerts: The wearable device activates its buzzer when the programmed alert conditions are met.
  • Data Monitoring: Recorded readings can be reviewed to follow changes over time.

This approach aims to make monitoring more personalized by focusing on changes relative to an individual's baseline rather than relying exclusively on universal reference values.

6. Main Features

  • Real-time sensor data monitoring.
  • Wireless communication between the wearable device and mobile application.
  • Personalized baseline configuration.
  • Automatic comparison of incoming readings against configured baseline values.
  • Deviation detection and visual alerts.
  • Audible alerts through the wearable buzzer.
  • Centralized dashboard for monitoring readings.
  • Historical data monitoring.
  • Movement and environmental monitoring.

7. NASA Research Connection

NASA research on wearable technology aboard the International Space Station demonstrates the importance of wearable monitoring for studying astronaut health, including heart activity, sleep, and exercise.

OrbitCare draws on this research context to explore an affordable, integrated wearable monitoring approach for future space exploration applications.

8. Benefits and Intended Impact

OrbitCare aims to demonstrate how wearable sensors, wireless communication, and connected software can support astronaut health awareness during space missions.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Bringing multiple monitoring indicators together in one platform.
  • Making physiological readings easier to access and monitor.
  • Identifying deviations from individual baseline values.
  • Providing visual and audible notifications when configured conditions are met.
  • Supporting future research into wearable health-monitoring solutions for long-duration space missions.

9. Creativity and Innovation

OrbitCare integrates multiple sensors, a wearable device, wireless communication, a backend system, and a dedicated mobile application into one connected monitoring solution.

Its main innovative aspect is the combination of personalized baseline monitoring, continuous sensor data collection, deviation detection, and intelligent alerts within a single wearable ecosystem.

Rather than simply displaying isolated sensor readings, OrbitCare connects data collection, processing, visualization, and alert generation into one integrated system.

10. Technologies and Tools Used

  • ESP32 Microcontroller.
  • MAX30102 Sensor.
  • MPU6050 Motion Sensor.
  • DHT11 Environmental Sensor.
  • OLED Display.
  • Wi-Fi Communication.
  • Embedded C++ for device programming.
  • Python and FastAPI for backend development.
  • React Native and Expo for mobile application development.
  • Visual Studio Code for software development and integration.

11. Future Development

Future improvements may include more accurate and spaceflight-compatible sensors, optimized wearable ergonomics, improved battery management, enhanced data analysis, and validation under simulated spaceflight conditions.

Further development could also explore integration with NASA research datasets and more advanced personalized monitoring algorithms.

12. Current Prototype Limitations

OrbitCare is an experimental prototype and not a certified medical device. Its sensor readings and alert thresholds have not been clinically validated. The configured baselines and deviation alerts are intended for demonstration and monitoring research, not medical diagnosis or decision-making.

The prototype has not been tested in actual spaceflight conditions.
